An independent enquiry committee has been constituted to investigate the allegations, stated the order.
Delhi University on Friday (November 13) cancelled the Ph.D. registration of Shubham Singh, a research scholar at its Faculty of Law, over allegations that he assaulted Anupam Jha, a professor at Law Centre-II, on August 17. The university also barred Mr. Singh from entering the campus, seeking admission to or appearing in any examination conducted by the university or its colleges for three years.
An order issued by DU Proctor Manoj Kumar Singh stated that an independent enquiry committee had been constituted to investigate the allegations. The incident allegedly took place around 10.30 a.m. at the entrance to Umang Bhawan on North Campus, following which Mr. Singh was suspended from his Ph.D. programme.
The committee, which submitted its report on September 9, emphasised the principle of “zero tolerance towards aggression, violence, and other forms of misconduct and suggested that all necessary measures be taken to safeguard a safe, secure, and respectful academic environment at the University of Delhi,” the order states.
The panel examined Mr. Jha’s complaint, CCTV footage, documentary records, a medico-legal case report and a written statement submitted by the Dean of the Faculty of Law. It also invited Mr. Singh to present his version of events.
According to the order, Mr. Singh was sent two emails inviting him for an online interaction. He responded to the second email using abusive and derogatory language but neither presented his account of the incident nor offered any clarification.
“Before taking a final decision, the university shared the committee’s report and recommendations with Mr. Singh on September 29, giving him seven days to submit his representation. Three more days were given to Mr. Singh through another email on October 6. However, he sent no response,” the order read.
The committee noted that Mr. Jha had no direct academic supervisory relationship with Mr. Singh and found no apparent circumstances that could justify the alleged misconduct. It also condemned the use of vulgar and inappropriate language towards committee members, including a woman professor.
